Nine striking sculptures by internationally acclaimed artists Gille and Marc will bring some of the world’s most endangered animals into the heart of Manchester this autumn, as ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ becomes part of Spinningfields.. . Each work creates an opportunity to encounter an endangered species in an unexpected and engaging way.. . ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ is part of Gille and Marc’s wider Love The Last project, a social movement driven by public art to raise awareness, funds and support for endangered animals around the world. Previous installations haven taken place across the world including the World Trade Centre in New York and Kingston and Chelsea Art Trail.. . Kayleigh Sheldon, Marketing Director, said: “Bringing ‘A Wild Life For Wildlife’ to Spinningfields is a perfect opportunity for our visitors to experience these incredible sculptures in the heart of Manchester. title: 8,000 free books to be given away on Bee Network today as city asked to ‘Take 10 to Read' | About Manchester
summary: A surprise is in store for passengers travelling on the Bee Network across Manchester today with 8,000 free books being handed out on the city’s trams and at bus interchanges to mark World Mental Health Day which falls on Saturday. With 6,000 free books up for grabs on the trams
lead: A surprise is in store for passengers travelling on the Bee Network across Manchester today with 8,000 free books being handed out on the city’s trams and at bus interchanges to mark World Mental Health Day which falls on Saturday.
practical_angle: Проверить, влияет ли это на поездки по Greater Manchester сегодня или в ближайшие дни.
raw_evidence: A surprise is in store for passengers travelling on the Bee Network across Manchester today with 8,000 free books being handed out on the city’s trams and at bus interchanges to mark World Mental Health Day which falls on Saturday With 6,000 free books up for grabs on the trams courtesy of Read Manchester, passengers of all ages might well find an inviting book on their seat this morning, waiting to be picked up by them when they sit down And with a further 2,000 free books being given out at bus interchanges across the wider city region by Greater Manchester Libraries, travellers across the whole network today can be sure of a good read as they ride The free book giveaway, which is in partnership with Transport for Greater Manchester, is part of Read Manchester’s ‘Take 10 to Read’ campaign which was first launched in the city in 2018 and is now promoted throughout the UK The campaign highlights the wellbeing benefits of reading and encourages people to spend just 10 minutes reading whenever they can, to help improve their mental health It complements wider work around the city by Read Manchester to encourage reading for enjoyment and help people discover the positive impact reading can have on learning, wellbeing and everyday life
